operative_text.controlling:
3.16(1)  An originating application for an order in the nature of
habeas corpus may be filed at any time and must be served under
rule 3.15(3) as soon as practicable after filing.
(2)  An affidavit or other evidence to be used to support the
originating application must be filed and served on each of the
other parties 10 days or more before the date scheduled for hearing
the application.

commentary.text:
Rule 3.16(1) mandates that an application for must be habeas corpus served “as soon as practicable”. That is consistent with the requirement that this process operate in an expedient manner. Once filed, applications receive a special habeas corpus priority treatment due to the timeliness requirement that is integral to the function of this special remedy. MacKinnon v. Bowden Institution, [2017] A.J. No. 987, 2017 ABQB 574 at para. 14 (Alta. Q.B.). 35 Part I of the , being Schedule B to the (U.K.), 1982, c. 11. Constitution Act, 1982 Canada Act 1982 36 Generally, see , [2019] S.C.J. No. Canada (Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness) v. Chhina 29, 2019 SCC 29 at para. 17 (S.C.C.); , [2014] S.C.J. No. 24, 2014 SCC 24 Mission Institution v. Khela at para. 30 (S.C.C.); , [2018] A.J. No. 265, 2018 ABQB 167 at paras. Philip v. Canada (Attorney General) 23-29 (Alta. Q.B.); and , [2017] A.J. No. 987, 2017 ABQB 574 paras. MacKinnon v. Bowden Institution 10-30 (Alta. Q.B.).
The ancient prerogative writ of ensures that deprivation of a person’s liberty habeas corpus is not unlawful. The writ is preserved and guaranteed by section 10(c) of the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms.35 In determining whether an application for habeas corpus should succeed, the court must consider: (1) whether the applicant has demonstrated deprivation of liberty; (2) whether a legitimate ground upon which to question legality of that deprivation has been raised; and (3) where a legitimate ground exists, whether the respondent can satisfy its onus to demonstrate that the detention decision was lawful.36 After the Supreme Court of Canada decision in , there has been an increase in Khela habeas corpus applications. As a result, the Court of King’s Bench of Alberta introduced an Accelerated Review Procedure where, before a hearing, the Crown may apply habeas corpus to strike the application under rule 3.68.37Then, through a document-only process,38the court will review the application and provide a preliminary assessment to either strike the habeas
